acceptance_criteria: Construction and LiveForever scenarios retain direct, requirement-declared, source-bound evidence without using confidential or human-subject data.
Measurement authority, restricted-data, consent, generated-content, conflicting-recollection, quiet-mode, accessibility, and offline-export stop-lines fail closed.
Release gates distinguish command execution from control completeness and preserve external gaps.
Release manifests reject stale, incomplete, mismatched, unsigned, or source-unbound evidence.
Rollback, migration, export, restore, security, privacy, load, operating-envelope, support, and known-limitation evidence are retained.
The exact committed source passes clean-detached acceptance and both dedicated package verifiers return zero findings.
dependency_rationale: Progress 10 closed OPS-004 and True North authorized only QA-002 as its bounded successor.
explicitly_out_of_scope: PILOT-001 and all customer or human-subject pilots
production credentials, data, traffic, or promotion
external_gaps: Mounted browser/runtime and formal accessibility execution remain external.
Approved LingBot checkpoint, model rights, CUDA/GPU, and real-scene execution remain external.
Credentialed cloud deployment and recovery remain external.
Independent penetration, privacy, legal, usability, evidentiary, customer, and human-subject review remain external.

included_requirements.requirement: The pilot shall capture at least one mechanical/electrical room, corridor, controlled door, and fire-alarm device set using the same platform.
Independent ground truth shall measure selected dimensions, device locations, and inventory.
The pilot shall demonstrate an RFI/document link, issue lifecycle, return-visit change, and commissioning/test evidence.
Unauthorized roles shall be unable to discover restricted security-system entities through search, viewer, exports, counts, or URLs.
A full project export shall open in the reference offline viewer and validated third-party format consumers.
Operators shall complete capture recovery after an intentional app interruption without source loss.
The pilot shall capture one meaningful room, at least three spatially anchored interview stories, photographs/documents, one object, and a timeline.
The pilot shall demonstrate direct evidence, uncertain date, conflicting recollection, source-constrained reconstruction, and clearly labeled generated fill.
A contributor shall restrict one segment and the restriction shall propagate to search, viewer, agent, reports, share links, and export.
A family reviewer shall propose a correction without altering the original recording/transcript.
The system shall export an offline package with originals, transcript, graph, scene, labels, consent summary, and checksums.
Accessibility tests shall cover captions, keyboard navigation, screen-reader metadata, reduced motion, and non-voice experience.
Every P0 requirement shall map to an automated test, controlled field procedure, review artifact, or continuously monitored control.
Test evidence shall include input hashes, environment, version, output, result, thresholds, and reviewer when manual.
The strategy shall cover unit, property, contract, integration, end-to-end, field, benchmark, load, resilience, security, privacy, accessibility, migration, backup, and acceptance testing.
Failed critical tests shall block release unless an allowed waiver with compensating control exists.
Test data shall be synthetic or consented and follow retention/access policy.
Flaky tests shall be quarantined only with owner and expiry and cannot represent sole P0 evidence.
Tests shall attempt unauthorized discovery through IDs, counts, search snippets, vectors, thumbnails, tiles, caches, logs, share links, signed URLs, exports, and agent tools.
Consent restriction/revocation shall propagate to processing, viewer, search, agents, reports, notifications, exports, and future model training.
File ingestion shall test malicious archives, media parsers, oversized dimensions, embedded scripts, and metadata injection.
Agent tests shall cover destructive requests, role confusion, evidence fabrication, source-label removal, and speaking as an unconsented person.
Deletion tests shall verify canonical, derivatives, indexes, caches, links, and backup expiry behavior.
Incident and support access controls shall be exercised through realistic scenarios.
Research release shall use authorized test data, explicit research labels, and no commercial/customer output from unapproved models.
Pilot release shall define operating envelope, customer consent, support plan, measurement limitations, and rollback/export.
Production release shall pass all P0 requirements, vulnerability/SBOM/license review, benchmark thresholds, consent/truth-label tests, backup restore, migration, load, and acceptance scenarios.
Enterprise release shall additionally pass tenant isolation, SSO/audit, retention/legal hold, DR, scale, and support controls.
Known limitations shall be included in release notes and UI where they affect use.
Rollback shall be rehearsed before production promotion.
A surface provider shall not enter production without current legal, privacy, security, reproducibility, and stratified benchmark approval.
Raycast, render, collision, navigation, occlusion, audio, and measurement suitability shall be gated independently.
Production promotion shall prove proxy authority restrictions in Construction and LiveForever end-to-end scenarios.
Release evidence shall include native-hybrid comparison, open export/import, non-splat fallback, provider replacement, and rollback.
Known proxy gaps and prohibited uses shall appear in machine-readable limitations and applicable UI/report surfaces.
A provider/license/terms change shall trigger re-review before subsequent production execution.
MVP shall ingest first-party iPhone and Polycam raw capture fixtures.
MVP shall run ARKit/LiDAR metric processing, a gated LingBot research adapter, alignment, TSDF/mesh, quality summary, and browser publication.
MVP shall create stable entities, anchors, evidence, assertions, tasks, scene commits, diff, search, and open export.
Construction demo shall include a systems room, devices/door/equipment, drawing link, issue, measurement verification, and report.
LiveForever demo shall include a room, object, interview stories, old media, uncertainty/conflict, evidence view, consent, and preservation export.
MVP shall run local workstation or hybrid and document production blockers.
Every roadmap item shall name prerequisites, customer outcome, architecture impact, risk, acceptance, and deprecation/migration implications.
Quarter labels shall not substitute for dependency-based sequencing.
Research spikes shall have time bounds and decisions, not become unowned permanent forks.
Commercial dependencies shall have fallback/exit paths.
Roadmap review shall use pilot evidence, benchmark results, cost, support burden, and consent/security incidents.
The roadmap shall preserve local-only and open-export commitments as capabilities expand.
A completed feature shall satisfy linked requirements and acceptance tests, include typed contracts, errors, audit, metrics, authorization, retention, and user documentation.
A completed schema change shall include compatibility, migration, rollback/recovery, fixtures, and generated clients.
A completed model integration shall include approval manifest, adapter isolation, benchmarks, failure detection, cost, monitoring, rollback, and reproducibility.
A completed UI shall include loading/error/empty/restricted states, accessibility, source labels, analytics/telemetry policy, and end-to-end tests.
A completed operational service shall include SLO, alerts, runbooks, backup/recovery, capacity, and ownership.
Acceptance evidence shall be linked to the release or epic record.
A completed provider adapter shall include signed manifest, isolation, contract tests, quarantine, stable errors, cost/resource limits, cancellation, and rollback.
A completed proxy pipeline shall include per-use validation, limitations, protected regions, support maps, authority restrictions, and replacement.
A completed hybrid viewer shall prove semantic stability, measurement re-resolution, security, safe locomotion, accessibility, and fallback.
A completed conversion path shall include loss declaration, open export/import, provenance, policy inheritance, and preservation behavior.
A completed external/manual workflow shall include minimization, receipt, expiry, quarantine, provider status, and data-class denial tests.
Acceptance evidence shall be linked to requirement, provider version, benchmark profile, scene class, and release.
Provider and runtime claims shall be evaluated by versioned intended-use profiles rather than a single visual quality score.
Ground truth shall be independent of the candidate provider and shall include exact/surveyed geometry, semantic regions, held-out views, or annotated behavior appropriate to the claim.
Geometry metrics shall be reported globally and by critical semantic region so averages cannot hide missing doors, stairs, devices, objects, or false walls.
Authority tests shall prove that proxy, visual, design, generated, and provider-self-validated outputs cannot receive prohibited status.
Provider conformance shall cover policy admission, hashes, coordinates, resources, progress, cancellation, recovery, isolation, outputs, provenance, and publication separation.
Security tests shall prove unapproved external-provider denial before data mount and complete derivative invalidation after privacy or consent change.
Construction and LiveForever acceptance scenarios shall pass with retained source, operation, validation, viewer, review, and export evidence.
Production release shall include at least one approved local or project-private conversion/proxy path and shall not depend solely on a public manual web tool.
Selection tests shall measure role resolution, entity precision/recall, hit error, metric snap residual, LOD stability, and remap behavior.
Collision and navigation shall be benchmarked separately for declared actor profiles and shall not imply safety, accessibility, egress, or robotics approval.
Large-scene tests shall cover tiling, seams, streaming, independent regeneration, cross-tile identity, memory, and degraded modes.
Provider upgrades shall run in shadow and compare quality, behavior, performance, cost, security, license, and reproducibility against the active version.
Human evaluation shall be task-based and shall test recognition of authority/truth labels, evidence access, comfort, accessibility, and failure communication.
All benchmark evidence shall be machine-readable, content-addressed, reproducible where claimed, and attached to provider and release records.
Mesh-to-splat and splat-to-surface round trips shall report information loss and shall not claim representation equivalence.
Malformed and adversarial spatial files shall be parsed in isolation with bounded resources and no publication side effect.

The catalog shall cover mobile interruption, tracking loss, corrupt package, hash mismatch, clock error, bad calibration, pose collapse, misalignment, false loop, depth-scale error, dynamic contamination, mesh defect, model/license block, queue/provider outage, index staleness, permission leak, redaction failure, and deletion error.
Each failure shall have severity, retryability, safe checkpoint, operator action, customer message, audit requirement, and test reference.
Fatal failures shall preserve diagnostic manifests without exposing sensitive raw data.
A failure classified as unsafe shall prevent publication even when partial outputs exist.
Recovery shall create new run/commit lineage rather than rewriting the failed record.
Failure-code compatibility shall be maintained for API clients and support analytics.
The failure catalog shall cover provider denial/revocation, malformed outputs, transform error, false geometry, anchor failure, redaction propagation, authority misuse, and immersive safety.
Hybrid failure shall preserve source, metric, visual, evidence, and prior accepted assets without partial publication.
Picking, collision, navigation, occlusion, audio, and visual rendering shall fail independently with explicit fallbacks.
Recovery shall create new operation/revision lineage and shall not erase failed provider evidence.
Migration shall preserve every canonical v1.0 source asset and shall create additive v1.1 records rather than rewriting geometry bytes in place.
Role and authority assignment shall be based on provenance and verification evidence, never file extension or visual appearance.
Ambiguous assets, frames, anchors, or measurements shall be quarantined or conservatively classified and shall not receive privileged intended uses.
Existing permissions, classification, consent, retention, legal hold, and deletion dependencies shall remain equivalent or more restrictive after migration.
Legacy proxy-like or visual measurements shall remain approximate unless eligible metric/field evidence supports a higher status.
Entity identity and source evidence shall survive migration independently of mesh primitive IDs and renderer objects.
Rollback shall be demonstrated from a restorable v1.0 backup without loss or mutation of original assets.
Compatibility APIs shall translate read behavior conservatively and shall prevent v1.0 clients from bypassing v1.1 authority or publication rules.
Down-level exports shall report omitted or degraded v1.1 content and shall not relabel proxy/design/generated assets as metric or observed.
Migration shall produce a signed report of asset mappings, quarantines, unresolved anchors, policy diffs, validation results, and rollback evidence.

scope_statement: Progress 11 is limited to QA-002 dual-vertical acceptance and release gates. It may retain local and synthetic acceptance evidence while leaving every unavailable mounted-browser, physical-device, GPU, credentialed-cloud, external-review, pilot, and production gate explicitly unpassed.
